Suryakand D. Lad . The Statutory Framework According to Section 4(1) of the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972, an employee is entitled to a gratuity upon termination of employment following at least five years of continuous service. Section 4(2) establishes the rate at fifteen days' wages for each completed year of service, or portion thereof exceeding six months, which must be paid by the employer. Thus, the question is decided by two definitions. According to Section 2(e), an employee is any person other than apprentices who is paid to perform any type of work in or related to an establishment covered by the Act for establishments owned or controlled by the Central or State Government, the person or authority designated for employee supervision and control (or the head of the Ministry or Department); for local authorities, the designated person or chief executive officer; and in any other situation, the person or authority having ultimate control over the establishment's affairs. The Controlling Authority may decide disputes and order the employer to pay under Section 7(4). The Contract Labour (Regulation and Abolition) Act, 1970, supplies the competing route. Section 21(1) makes the contractor responsible for wages, while Section 21(4) makes the principal employer liable to pay wages in full, or the unpaid balance, where the contractor defaults, with a right to recover from the contractor by deduction or as a debt. However, the term principal employer or contractor is not mentioned in the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972. Whether gratuity is included under the definition of "wages" turns on Section 2(vi) of the Payment of Wages Act, 1936, which includes sums payable on termination under any law but excludes gratuity. items.title: Related Party Transactions: A governance priority for Indian companies
items.summary: In today's interconnected business environment, related party transactions ("RPTs") are a normal and often necessary part of business operations. Companies regularly transact with subsidiaries, associate companies, joint ventures, promoters, directors and key managerial personnel to improve operational efficiency and leverage group synergies. The challenge is not the existence of RPTs, but ensuring that they are conducted transparently, on fair commercial terms, and with appropriate oversight. When managed properly, RPTs can support business objectives. When they are not, they can create conflicts of interest, regulatory concerns and reputational risks. This makes an effective RPT framework a critical component of good corporate governance. Regulatory Framework The regulation of RPTs in India is primarily driven by the Companies Act, 2013 and the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015. The Companies Act adopts a broad definition of a "related party" and covers directors, their relatives, key managerial personnel, entities in which they hold an interest and companies under common control. Section 188 of the Act prescribes the approval requirements for specified related party transactions. Transactions that are both in the ordinary course of business and on arm's length terms are generally exempt from Board and shareholder approval requirements under that provision. In addition, all RPTs require Audit Committee oversight under Section 177, while directors are required to disclose their interests under Section 184. Listed entities face additional compliance requirements under the Listing Regulations, including: Adoption of a policy on material RPTs and dealing with RPTs; Prior Audit Committee approval of RPTs; Shareholder approval for material RPTs; and Periodic disclosures to stock exchanges and investors. The regulatory framework has also expanded the scope of who may be considered a related party, reflecting the increasing focus on transparency and investor protection. Compliance is more than obtaining approvals Many organisations view RPT compliance as a documentation exercise that begins only when a transaction is ready for execution. This approach often results in missed approvals, delayed transactions and disclosure gaps. A bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant , Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana was hearing a batch of petitions arising from the October protests in Delhi against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar. "You cannot occupy a site for all times to come. There are other protesters. Where will the farmers go? Where will the workers go? Where will the trade unions go? Where will the homeless go? items.title: File a petition: Delhi High Court refuses suo motu case against ACP Manasvi Vashishta for threats to lawyers
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Tuesday refused to take suo motu cognisance of alleged threats made by Delhi Police officer Manasvi Vashishta against lawyers. Vashishta was seen on video making remarks against lawyers and warning "goon in black coats" of serious repercussions. A Division Bench of acting Chief Justice (ACJ) Nitin Wasudeo Sambre and Justice Sanjay Sharma asked lawyers to file a formal petition and assured that the issue will be looked into. A group of lawyers had mentioned the matter before the acting Chief Justice. Lawyers told the Court that remarks like the use of AK47 and "Kaale coat ke Gunde (goons in black coats)" were used against lawyers. "You [Acting Chief Justice] are our chief. If you take suo motu cognisance we will be assured," the lawyers told the Bench today. However, the Court asked the lawyers to file a formal petition and assured them that the Court will direct its listing and look into it. "You file a formal petition. We will look into it. We will order its listing. Give a copy to the Standing Counsel (Criminal) Sanjay Lao. I assure you that we will look into it. You give representation, but also file a formal petition," the court told the lawyers. Acting Chief Justice Nitin Wasudeo Sambre, Justice Sanjay Sharma The dispute between ACP Manasvi Vashishta and Delhi lawyers began after advocate Lalit Bansal suffered a serious head injury during an alleged assault on October 23. Lawyers subsequently visited Shahdara police station, alleging that Vashishta and the Station House Officer (SHO) had assured them that the accused would be arrested but later released them. When advocates returned to question the police action, Vashishta allegedly brandished his revolver and threatened them. The incident triggered an indefinite strike by district court lawyers, who demanded action against the officers. Vashishta and SHO Arun Kumar were transferred on October 28, following which lawyers called off their strike. Further controversy erupted on November 2 when ACP Vashishtha and Delhi Police personnel protested outside police headquarters against the transfers. During the demonstration, certain remarks were also made about the lawyers. Vashishta has now been suspended by the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA).

items.title: Ram Mandir donation theft probe: Supreme Court ends monitoring after police files chargesheet
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday closed a batch of petitions related to the Ayodhya Ram Mandir fund embezzlement case after it was informed that the police has filed a chargesheet in the case. A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said the petitioners, who had approached the top court to seek an independent probe into the case, can assist the trial court where the matter is now pending. "It is not a simple case of an accused versus the State. It is a case where some element of public interest is also involved. Therefore, we will grant you, like the law now permits the victims of crime, to assist the Court," the Court said. Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana The Court directed the trial court to proceed in accordance with law. "Since there is an element of public interest involved, the petitioner is granted liberty to assist the Court of learned Judicial Magistrate on the same premise as the law enables a victim of crime to assist the Court," it added. A batch of petitions before the Court were filed seeking a CBI probe in the donation theft case. However, the Court allowed an SIT of police officers, with the addition of a forensic auditor, to continue investigating the matter. The SIT found 105 instances of unauthorised currency removal and suspicious deposits linked to eight accused. Today, Solicitor General Tushar Mehta informed the Court that the accused would invest the money or deposit it in bank accounts. "We went back in time to see how much money was deposited. items.summary: A petition has been filed before the Supreme Court seeking directions to the Chief Justice of India and the Central government to finalise the Memorandum of Procedure (MoP) laying down the procedure for appointment of judges to High Courts and the Supreme Court The plea filed by NGO Loka Prahari states that appointment of judges to constitutional courts should be based on the unanimous view of the Collegium taking into consideration factors mentioned in the top court's 2015 judgment in NJAC case . The plea has also sought directions to bring the Collegium decisions within the purview of the Right to Information Act (RTI Act). The matter came up for hearing on Monday before a bench of Justices PS Narasimha and Alok Aradhe when the former chose to recuse from the case. Justice PS Narasimha and Justice Alok Aradhe Justice Narasimha said that he had appeared as an Additional Solicitor General in a similar case related to MoP. The MoP was first drafted in June 1999 pursuant to the directions of the Supreme Court in the Second Judges case. It laid down the procedure to be followed under the Collegium system for appointing judges to the higher judiciary. In 2015, the Parliament enacted the National Judicial Appointments Commission (NJAC) Act to mark a significant shift in the manner of the appointment of judges. The NJAC Act sought to replace the collegium system by providing for a body comprising representatives from both the judiciary and the Centre to make recommendations for the appointment of judges to the higher judiciary. However, a Constitution Bench of the Supreme Court, on October 16, 2015, struck down the NJAC as unconstitutional for violating independence of judiciary. Subsequently, for the first time ever, the Court invited suggestions for improving the Collegium system of appointing judges with the object of ensuring greater transparency in judicial appointments. Based on the inputs received, the Court on December 16, 2015 passed an order by which it left the task of amending the Memorandum of Procedure (MoP) to the central government. During the initial phase after the NJAC judgment, the MoP did not materialise due to disagreements between the Centre and the Collegium. items.title: Mercedes crash: Kerala court to hold in-camera hearing of appeals against bail granted to accused minor
items.summary: A sessions court in Kerala on Monday decided to hold in-camera hearings of the appeals against the bail granted to the minor accused of driving a Mercedes-Benz car and killing a scooterist. The 17-year-old accused, the son of an additional district judge, was driving a Mercedes-Benz car when he hit a two-wheeler in Kochi's Cheranalloor in the early hours of October 25, killing the scooterist, one Jayabalakrishnan. Ernakulam Additional District and Sessions Judge Kavitha Gangadharan on Saturday criticised the police for not acting against social media posts that revealed the minor's identity. Section 74 of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015, prohibits the disclosure of the identity of a child in conflict with law (CCL), except with the permission of the competent authority. The Court had, therefore, directed the cyber police to take action against all posts revealing the teenager's identity. When the appeals moved by the State and the victim's family against the bail granted to the minor was taken up today, the Court deemed it fit to continue the hearing in-camera, to further ensure the privacy of the Child in Conflict with the Law (CCL). Kavita Gangadharan The accused teenager was initially booked for the offences of rash driving and causing death by negligence under Sections 281 and 106(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (BNS). The accused teenager was granted bail by the Juvenile Justice Board (JJB) on October 26. After continued protests by the victim's family and local residents, the police added more serious offences punishable under Section 105 (culpable homicide not amounting to murder) BNS read with Sections 181, 183, 199A(1) and 199A(2) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (MVA). The FIR also named the father of the teenager, an additional district judge who is currently posted at the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (MACT) at Iranjalakuda in Thrissur district, as a co-accused. items.title: The New Indian Express moves Supreme Court against Bombay HC barring its events outside South India
items.summary: Express Publications (Madurai), publisher of The New Indian Express, has moved the Supreme Court challenging a Bombay High Court judgment that restrained it from using the New Indian Express trademark for promotional activities outside five southern States and certain Union Territories. A Bench of Justices JB Pardiwala and Manmohan on Monday appeared disinclined to interfere with the High Court's judgment, observing that the High Court had passed an exhaustive order. items.title: Nobody will trust you: Supreme Court slams Centre for stalling enforcement of 2004, 2016 arbitral awards
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday criticised the Central government for frustrating the enforcement of decades-old foreign arbitral awards in favour of Vedanta Limited and Ravva Oil (Singapore) Pte Limited, warning that such litigation would undermine confidence in India's arbitration regime. [GoI v. Vedanta] A Bench of Justices JB Pardiwala and Manmohan questioned the government's approach to enforcing arbitral awards while hearing its challenge to a Delhi High Court judgment permitting enforcement of awards passed in 2004 and 2016. " What are these arguments? You are frustrating an arbitral award like this? At the stage of enforcement of it? " the Court remarked. The Bench also questioned the government's commitment to arbitration, referring to discussions about arbitration at conferences and seminars even as parties continued to resist enforcement of awards. " And we talk about all of this arbitration and seat and this and that ," the Court observed. The Bench warned the government that such litigation could erode confidence in the arbitration process. The award was eventually upheld by the Malaysian Federal Court in 2011. In July 2014, the government issued show-cause notices seeking recovery of approximately $99 million from the companies. items.title: Allahabad High Court directs State to pay ₹1.25 lakh to man for 5-day illegal detention
items.summary: The Allahabad High Court recently ordered the State to pay a compensation of ₹1.25 lakh to a man who was unlawfully detained for five days at a police station [ Gyanti Devi And 2 Others v State of UP & 3 Others ]. A bench of Justice Atul Sreedharan and Justice Achal Sachdev observed that the investigating officer, who had detained the man, demonstrated an "arrogance of authority" by not following the procedure established by law. "The manner in which the I.O. has demonstrated his arrogance of authority, by detaining petitioner No.2 for full five days without even thinking twice and without following the procedure established by law, makes it appear that he considered it business as usual," the Court said. It added that the harshest punishment should be imposed upon the errant errant police officer in case he is found guilty in a departmental inquiry initiated by the police department in the matter. The Court proceeded to order the payment of ₹1.25 lakh to the person who was detained illegally for five days. "This Court is of the opinion that, for the period of five days undergone by petitioner No.2 in custody without adherence to the procedure established by law, compensation at the rate of Rs.25,000/- per day is granted, which amounts to Rs.1,25,000/-. This shall not preclude the right of petitioner No.2 to sue the Police Department in an action in tort for damages," the Court directed. The Court further said that the compensation paid should be recovered from the police officers found guilty of having carried out the illegal detention. "The compensation granted to the petitioner shall be recovered from such persons who, after an inquiry, are found guilty of having detained him. The State may effect such recovery, if so desired," it said. Justice Atul Sreedharan and Justice Achal Sachdev The Court passed the order on a habeas corpus petition moved by one Gyanti Devi who said her son Chandan Rajbhar was detained by the police after he eloped with an 18-year-old woman. An FIR registered in Deoria under Section 87 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita alleged that the woman was kidnapped with the intention of compelling her to enter into a marriage. Rajbhar was taken into custody by Salempur police in district Deoria on August 28. He remained under illegal detention before he was formally arrested on September 2. items.title: Indian scientist secures patent for in-vivo power generator after Bombay High Court order against IIT
items.summary: The Indian Patent Office has formally approved a patent for scientist Dr. Tarkeshwar Chandrakant Patil, securing his exclusive ownership over an invention capable of generating electrical power inside the human body. This outcome follows a September 8 order of the Bombay High Court in Patil’s decade-long dispute with the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Bombay. The dispute involved an apparatus and a method for in-vivo power generation, a technology designed to keep medical implants active inside the human body. Patil’s patented device functions by converting glucose found in cerebrospinal fluid into a hydrogen-rich fuel, such as ethanol or methanol, using bioenzymes. This fuel powers a nano-scale biofuel cell implanted in the body, creating a self-sustaining power source that mitigates the need for repeated surgeries to replace traditional lithium-ion button batteries. IIT Bombay initially filed the patent application in August 2013. However, after internal disputes, the institute executed a worldwide assignment deed in 2017 transferring all intellectual property rights to Patil. Despite the transfer, IIT-B contested his rights in India, leading to a prolonged delay in him getting the patent. The High Court recently criticised it as a systematic frustration of a premier scientist. Thus, in its order of September 8, the High Court declared Dr. Patil as the original inventor of the patent and directed a Deputy Controller of Patents and Designs to recognize him as the applicant in a patent application filed by IIT Bombay (IITB) in 2013. On October 30, the Assistant Controller of Patents & Designs Aditya Venkateswara NC executed the Court's mandate by substituting Patil as the sole applicant and inventor and set aside the July 2025 rejection. The Controller also dismissed pending technical objections regarding the invention's inventive step. items.title: Courts reviewing arbitral award on merits defeats purposes of arbitration: Chief Justice Vibhu Bahkru
items.summary: Karnataka High Court Chief Justice Vibhu Bakhru on Saturday said that allowing courts to undertake a full merit-based review of arbitral awards would defeat the fundamental purpose of arbitration, which was intended to provide parties with a final adjudication of disputes outside the traditional court system. Speaking at a conference on Ethics and Evidence in Arbitration in Bengaluru, Justice Bakhru acknowledged concerns over the quality of arbitral awards but cautioned against expanding judicial scrutiny. " But if you have a full merits review then automatically the private arbitration is over ," Justice Bakhru said. The conference was jointly hosted by the London Court of International Arbitration (LCIA), ArbitralWomen and the Arbitration and Conciliation Centre Bengaluru at the Karnataka Judicial Academy. Justice Bakhru made the observation during a fireside conversation with Senior Advocate Shashank Garg , a Court Member of the LCIA, on the hits and misses of India's arbitration landscape. Garg referred to a debate over whether challenges to arbitral awards under Section 34 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act should permit a more extensive examination of disputes on their merits. Section 34 provides limited grounds for setting aside arbitral awards, including violations of public policy, patent illegality in domestic awards and procedural irregularities. It does not ordinarily permit courts to reconsider disputes as appellate courts would. Justice Bakhru said that demands for broader judicial scrutiny stemmed from dissatisfaction with the quality of some awards. " The quality of awards is not coming up to the standard that you can sit back and say, no, let us review. It is a vicious circle ," he observed. He explained that limited judicial interference depended on arbitrators delivering well-reasoned awards that inspired confidence. When arbitrators delivered high-quality awards, courts could adopt a hands-off approach and refrain from interfering with them, he observed. However, he emphasised that arbitration was founded on the understanding that arbitrators chosen by parties would finally adjudicate their disputes. " It is the arbitrators that people the parties choose are the final adjudicators of the dispute ," he said. items.title: Bhushan Power: NCLT rejects promoters’ challenge to maintainability of government's recovery plea
items.summary: The National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) rejected the challenge raised by Bhushan Power and Steel Limited’s (BPSL) former promoters and others to the maintainability of the petition filed by Central government seeking recovery of ₹5,431 crore allegedly diverted from the company. [Union of India Vs BPSL] President Justice Anupinder Singh Grewal and Technical Member Ravindra Chaturvedi held that insolvency resolution and replacement of management did not bar proceedings against those allegedly retaining diverted funds. “ The replacement of the erstwhile management may have brought its control over the company to an end, but it does not, by itself, undo the alleged diversion or remove the prejudice that may have been caused to the company and the public interest, ” the Bench said. The October 30 order dismissed eight applications challenging the maintainability of the government's plea. The applicants included former promoters Sanjay Singal and Aarti Singal, their daughter Priyanka Miglani, associated companies and other individuals. The tribunal confined its decision to whether the petition could be entertained. “ We reiterate that no finding has been recorded on the merits of the allegations, which remain to be adjudicated, ” it clarified. The Union government, through the Serious Fraud Investigation Office (SFIO), filed the petition under Sections 241(2), 242 and 246 read with Section 339 of the Companies Act, 2013. Relying on an SFIO investigation report dated May 6, 2022, it sought to hold the respondents personally liable for at least ₹5,431 crore, besides interest. It also sought attachment and realisation of their assets. The SFIO alleged that funds were siphoned off from BPSL through entities controlled by its former promoters. The transactions allegedly involved routing funds to maintain the debt-equity ratio required for bank financing and purchasing movable and immovable properties. BPSL entered insolvency proceedings in July 2017 and was acquired by JSW Steel in March 2021. items.title: How Bengaluru’s drag performers are building community, one song at a time
items.summary: Izzy B is a 26-year-old drag queen born and raised in Bengaluru. Drag was not something she had set out to do. It was her curiosity about queer spaces that led to her first queer party in 2022. “I saw these beautiful queens, dressing up, with wigs and beautiful makeup, lashes and everything, and I was fascinated,” she says, recalling the first few drag performances she witnessed. Izzy started loving the art form when she saw another drag queen, Cologne Doll, perform. “I saw her on the stage of Kitty Ko (a queer-friendly nightclub in Bengaluru), and I was like, this is so good, I love it.” Drag is a performance and visual art, rooted in queer subculture. Drag performances often involve exaggerated traditional gender expressions to challenge the same. Performances usually feature drag queens or drag kings who dress in clothing associated with the opposite sex or otherwise. Performers choose a drag name or a stage name based on their interests and build a unique drag persona. A drag performer can be cis, trans, non-binary, or any sexuality; the persona performed on stage can also differ from how someone identifies off stage. Miss Bhenji, who is now Izzy’s drag mother, is known for her quirkiness. “I saw Miss Bhenji being all quirky on the stage and I related that to myself,” Izzy says. A drag mother is a senior drag queen who shelters and mentors their drag children. “And slowly things started becoming familiar, and I could see myself performing.” After Kitty Ko's auditions, Izzy got her first show in July 2024. “The show was a hit. People loved me instantly. People know me for twerking, and they recognise me as Izzy B, the twerking diva.” Izzy found her joy, but that didn’t last long. Having been born and raised in Bengaluru and still living with her family, Izzy was hesitant to do drag as she came from a family steeped in religious orthodoxy and the idea of performing drag felt like a risk. As Izzy was practising, only for her third show, her biological mother saw her. What Izzy had been dreading actually happened. For almost eight months, Izzy was shut in — not allowed out of the house. “My performance was also very sensual, and they have never seen their son doing these things . And it was quite a hectic period.” She was staying with her family, had nowhere else to go, and depended on them financially. “So I had no choice but to accept what was happening, and I stopped performing,” she says, eyes welling up. items.title: Delhi Police seeks to silence digital rights groups IFF, SFLC on X, wants accounts removed
items.summary: The Delhi police has issued two notices to social media platform X, seeking the removal of the accounts of digital rights organisations Internet Freedom Foundation (IFF) and Software Freedom Law Center (SFLC) apart from the operator of GeoBlockedIndia, over allegations of defamation against the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS). IFF is a digital rights advocacy organisation that defends against threats to civil liberties and democracy in India, and SFLC is a donor-supported legal services and policy organisation founded in 2010 that protects digital freedom, privacy and civil liberties in India. The IFF on Tuesday, November 3, said it would approach the court if the Delhi Police does not withdraw the notices, which also seek removal of 37 posts, including content published by 16 other users. IFF said it received copies of the two police notices from X on the morning of November 3. The notices were filed by the Special Commissioner of Police (Crime), Delhi Police, on October 31 and November 2, 2026. According to IFF, the first notice was submitted to X on October 31 at 8.06 pm. It identified two posts published by IFF and SFLC on October 30 concerning a legal notice purportedly issued on behalf of the RSS. The Delhi Police reportedly described the posts as “defamatory towards the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh under Section 356 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023” and sought their removal or withholding. The second notice was submitted on November 2 at 8.51 am and listed 40 URLs. These included 37 individual posts and the entire X accounts of IFF, SFLC and GeoBlockedIndia. The provisions cited in the Delhi Police notices relate to criminal defamation and the removal of unlawful online content. The stated reason in the second notice read: “The posts constitute defamation and illegal content under Section 356 BNS. Under Rule 3(1)(d) of the IT Rules, 2021, read with Section 79(3)(b) IT Act, lawful notices require action within 3 hours.” Section 356 of the BNS deals with criminal defamation and prescribes punishment for statements made with the intention of harming a person’s reputation. Rule 3(1)(d) of the IT Rules lays down the procedure for intermediaries, including social media platforms, to remove or disable access to unlawful content following legally recognised government or court directions. Students from at least four colleges attended Union Home Minister Amit Shah’s rally in Hyderabad on Monday, November 2. The Union Home Minister was leading a Mahapadayatra to protest Congress leader Rahul Gandhi’s stance against Election Commission-mandated Special Intensive Revision (SIR). One of the colleges felt duped and said they permitted their students to attend the rally because they were misled by a local BJP leader. Around 60-70 National Cadet Corps (NCC) students enrolled in Hyderabad’s Pragathi Mahavidyalaya and 250-270 students from Moinabad’s Karuna School of Nursing were present at the rally. Around 40-50 students from Akshara Junior College and 83 students from Shantiniketan women’s college were also in attendance. The BJP OBC Morcha, BJP minority cell headed by Jagmohan Singh and the party’s medical cell headed by Dr Koppula Rajasekhar Reddy were also present at the rally. However, several students TNM spoke to said they were brought to the two-hour rally by the college authorities. items.title: Telangana man who helped Bondi Beach shooting victims alleges land grab attempt
items.summary: Follow TNM ’ s WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. Hyderabad-born cab driver Rahmat Pasha, who helped rescue people injured at Bondi Beach shooting in Sydney, has alleged that a group of persons are trying to encroach upon the land owned by his family in Vikarabad. He also accused Congress MLC Balmoor Venkat of using his political influence to help encroachers. Venkat has denied the allegation. The Bondi beach incident happened in December 2025 and a father-son duo were charged with mass shooting at the public resulting in 16 deaths. In a video circulating on social media, Rahmat alleged that a group of people had been harassing his family for nearly six years over a 5.5-acre plot owned by his 75-year-old father, Mohammed Azmath Pasha, in Alampally village located near the New Civil Hospital. Rahmat alleged that the group was attempting to lay a road through the property despite a court order protecting his father's possession. Speaking to TNM, Rahmat said that despite police complaints, no action was taken. He also accused the police of pressuring his father to permit the road work and making him sit at the police station for several hours. Questioning the government's handling of the dispute, Rahmat said that the MLC was using his position via his associates including Rahmat’s own relative Aslam Feroze to target his elderly father. Responding to the allegations, Aslam Feroze accused Rahmat’s family of trying to prevent the construction of a building approved by the Directorate of Town and Country Planning. “The property was divided by Azmat Pasha himself and I legally own the piece of land on which I am constructing. Despite this, there is a legal hurdle,” he said. Aslam further said a relative who was helping him reached out to Venkat Balmoor for assistance. TNM reached out to MLC Venkat but he denied the allegations. “I don’t even know Rahmat Pasha or his family. The Sanathnagar area division president for the Congress party, Muzzamil got involved because he knows the family. Upon learning about the issue, I asked Muzzamil to stay out of it as it was a family dispute. I have nothing whatsoever to do with this issue,” Venkat told TNM. items.title: Bloodstains, empty classrooms and fear: Andhra school struggles after chainsaw attack
items.summary: The haphazardly discarded shoes, scattered books and lumps of partly dried blood are enough to send a chill down anyone's spine. Inside this classroom at the Zilla Parishad High School in Rapthadu in Andhra Pradesh’s Anantapur district, a 21-year-old man walked in carrying a chainsaw and attacked a 15-year-old girl, leaving her critically injured. Another student who tried to protect her was also wounded. The brutal attack on October 31 has since triggered outrage across the state. The classroom remains closed as a crime scene. But the evidence of the horror that unfolded here is still visible. The blood splattered across the floor, the belongings left behind in haste and the images of the attack offer a grim reminder of what the students and teachers witnessed. On October 31, at around 10.30 am, while a lesson was underway, the accused, identified as Hemanth alias Dummu, entered Class 10 carrying a running chainsaw and attacked Gopika, a student. She suffered severe injuries to her face, neck and abdomen, and her right hand was nearly severed. Lakshmi, another student, was injured when she tried to intervene and save her friend. Hemanth fled the school, leaving the chainsaw behind. The horrific attack has left parents and students deeply shaken, a fear reflected in the poor attendance when the school reopened on Monday, November 2. Only around five students had turned up, most of them boys. The school gate, which had earlier been unsecured, was now guarded by three people. Anyone entering the premises had to establish their identity. The classroom has been sealed off as a crime scene until the investigation concludes. “We are very scared now,” a teacher standing guard at the gate said. Among the few students who came to school, some were offered a demonstration of amateur self-defence techniques. The instructor explained certain pressure points that could incapacitate a potential assailant. The boys giggled among themselves, seemingly unconvinced by the exercise.
